basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 4.' and it opens '(Vers. 4.) Gigantes autem erant super terram in diebus illis, et post haec quomodo'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 4.) Gigantes autem erant super terram in diebus illis, et post haec quomodo ingrediebantur filii Dei ad filias hominum, et generabant eis. Illi erant gigantes a saeculo homines nominati. In Hebraeo ita habet: Cadentes erant in terra in diebus illis, id est, ANNAPHILIM (הנפלים). Et post haec ut ingrediebantur filii deorum ad filias hominum, et generabant eis: hi erant fortes a principio viri nominati. Pro cadentibus, sive gigantibus, violentos interpretatus est Symmachus. Et angelis autem et sanctorum liberis convenit nomen cadentium.
